messages.content: What does the paper say about recall at small index sizes?
Recall stays above 0.95 up to a million vectors with the default graph settings. Below ten thousand vectors a flat scan is as fast as the graph, so the index switches to it.
Which setting trades speed for recall?
The search width (`ef_search`). Raising it visits more of the graph on each query: recall goes up and so does the time per query.
Compare the three index types, and show how to set the search width.

The graph index answers fastest at the same recall; the flat scan needs no build at all.

| Index | Build time | Query time | Recall at 10 | Memory per vector | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flat | none | 41 ms | 1.00 | 1.5 KB | under 10,000 vectors |
| IVF | 3 min | 6 ms | 0.93 | 1.6 KB | batch updates |
| Graph (HNSW) | 9 min | 2 ms | 0.97 | 2.1 KB | interactive search |

Set the search width when you open the index:

```rust
let index = Index::open("papers.idx")?;
index.set_ef_search(128);
let hits = index.search(&query, 10)?;
```
Summarise the reading group notes from Tuesday.
The group agreed to compare graph and IVF indexes on the same corpus, and to read the quantisation paper next.
Which papers cite the product quantisation paper?
Four papers in your library cite it; two of them extend it to graph indexes.
